tracks.title: Staff Engineer Interview Prep
tracks.summary: System design, ownership stories, and production AI depth for Staff loops.
outcomes: Tell Staff-level ownership stories with metrics
Design distributed systems with clear tradeoffs
Explain production AI guardrails (entitlements, audit, evals)
study_plan: Day 1–2: Rewrite 3 ownership stories (Context → Action → Metric)
Day 3–4: Drill 2 system designs (sync engine, NLQ platform)
Day 5: Mock behavioral + deep dive on one production AI project
Day 6–7: Timed answers + tighten resume bullets to stories

tracks.title: Engineering Manager Interview Prep
tracks.summary: People leadership, delivery, hiring, and vendor/team-build narratives.
outcomes: Lead with people + delivery ownership, not only IC craft
Run hiring / performance / incident stories cleanly
Show technical credibility without competing for IC tickets
study_plan: Day 4: Hiring loop + performance management scenarios
Day 5–7: Mock HM screen + conflict / prioritization drills

tracks.title: Java → Production AI Upskilling
tracks.summary: Practical path from Spring services to RAG, agents, and safe LLM features.
outcomes: Map Spring concepts to FastAPI / AI service patterns
Explain RAG vs fine-tuning vs prompt-only clearly
Design an entitlement-safe NLQ or document pipeline
study_plan: Week 2: RAG building blocks (chunk, embed, retrieve, cite)
Week 4: Ship a tiny production-shaped AI feature

tracks.title: Java → Python Developer
tracks.summary: Map Java/Spring instincts to Python: syntax, typing, OOP, asyncio, and FastAPI.
outcomes: Translate Java types and collections into idiomatic Python
Use typing, venv/packaging, and pytest like a production Python engineer
Explain Spring concepts as FastAPI + Pydantic equivalents
study_plan: Day 3: Classes, dataclasses, protocols vs Java interfaces
Day 5: asyncio vs executors; when to use each
Day 6–7: Rebuild a small Spring-style API in FastAPI and practice explaining it

tracks.title: Java
tracks.summary: Core Java, concurrency, Spring Boot, and production service patterns.
outcomes: Explain OOP, collections, and concurrency clearly
Design Spring Boot APIs with solid error handling
Talk JVM memory, threads, and performance tradeoffs
study_plan: Day 5: Spring Boot REST, validation, transactions
Day 6–7: Practice debugging and production failure scenarios

tracks.title: Python
tracks.summary: Python fundamentals, typing, async, and packaging for real services.
outcomes: Write clean typed Python with clear module structure
Explain GIL, async/await, and when to use each
Build FastAPI-style request/response flows

tracks.title: JavaScript
tracks.summary: Modern JS: language essentials, async, DOM, and browser APIs.
outcomes: Master closures, prototypes, and this-binding
Use promises/async-await confidently
Manipulate the DOM and handle events cleanly
study_plan: Day 6–7: DOM events and small UI scripts

tracks.title: TypeScript
tracks.summary: Types, generics, utility types, and typing React/Node apps.
outcomes: Model domain data with interfaces and unions
Use generics and utility types effectively
Type API responses and component props safely
study_plan: Day 5–7: Type a small React + API client

tracks.title: React
tracks.summary: Components, hooks, state, effects, and production React patterns.
outcomes: Build components with clean props and state
Use effects correctly without common bugs
Explain rendering, keys, and performance basics
study_plan: Day 6–7: Forms, errors, and a mini feature

tracks.title: Node.js
tracks.summary: Node runtime, Express/Fastify APIs, async I/O, and packaging.
outcomes: Explain event loop and non-blocking I/O
Build REST APIs with middleware and validation
Handle errors, env config, and basic security
study_plan: Day 1–2: Modules, npm, event loop basics

tracks.title: HTML
tracks.summary: Semantic HTML, forms, accessibility, and document structure.
outcomes: Use semantic tags for structure and SEO
Build accessible forms and navigation
Understand HTML5 APIs at a practical level
study_plan: Day 5–7: Accessibility checklist + rebuild a landing section

tracks.title: CSS
tracks.summary: Layout, flex/grid, responsive design, and modern styling patterns.
outcomes: Build layouts with Flexbox and Grid
Make responsive UIs with media queries
Use variables, specificity, and clean organization
study_plan: Day 6–7: Recreate a card/hero section pixel-clean

questions.prompt: Tell me about a system you owned end-to-end. What was hard, what did you decide, and what measurable outcome did you drive?
hints: End with a metric (uptime, latency, manual hours saved)

questions.prompt: Design a customer data syncing engine that must move large volumes of data to destinations reliably. How would you approach batch today and streaming later?
hints: Call out multi-tenant isolation and failure modes

questions.prompt: How would you ship an enterprise natural-language-to-SQL feature safely when different customers must never see each other's data?
Give your 30–40 second introduction as an Engineering Manager. Include scope, signature wins, and what you're looking for next.
hints: One transformation win + one AI/product win

questions.prompt: Describe leading a vendor-to-in-house transition. How did you protect delivery and uptime while building the team?
Product wants more features; your team is drowning in reliability work. How do you handle the conflict?
You're a Java/Spring engineer. Explain how you would structure a production AI feature service and what maps from Spring Boot patterns.
When would you use RAG instead of fine-tuning, and how would you evaluate whether retrieval quality is good enough?
hints: Eval with golden questions + citation checks

questions.prompt: Design a simple document extraction agent for messy Excel/PDF inputs. What steps, tools, and failure handling do you need?
Explain encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism with a realistic Spring service example.
hints: Prefer composition when inheritance gets messy

questions.prompt: How would you parallelize independent I/O-bound tasks in Java without blocking the request thread carelessly?
Design a Spring Boot REST endpoint that validates input, calls a service, and returns consistent error responses.
Why use type hints in Python services, and how do dataclasses/pydantic help API boundaries?
When should you use asyncio in Python, and what mistakes do people make with blocking calls inside async functions?
hints: Do not block the event loop

questions.prompt: Sketch a FastAPI endpoint that accepts JSON, validates it, and returns a typed response model.
Explain closures with a practical example (e.g. private counters or event handlers).
Compare callbacks, promises, and async/await. When does Promise.all matter?
How would you build a small interactive UI (toggle + list render) with vanilla JS and event delegation?
hints: Delegate from parent for dynamic lists

questions.prompt: Explain union types and type narrowing with an example of API success vs error responses.
Write (in words or pseudocode) a generic fetchJson<T>() helper and explain the type parameter.
hints: Validate at runtime separately if needed

questions.prompt: How do you type React props and state for a form component with optional fields?
When do you lift state up vs keep it local? Give a concrete UI example.
hints: Avoid prop drilling with context carefully

questions.prompt: What are common useEffect mistakes, and how do you fetch data safely in React?
hints: Prefer frameworks or query libs for caching

questions.prompt: Why are keys important in lists, and what goes wrong if you use array index as key during reordering?
hints: State can attach to wrong item

questions.prompt: Explain the Node.js event loop in practical terms. What happens if you run CPU-heavy work on the main thread?
Design an Express (or similar) REST API with middleware for logging, auth, and centralized error handling.
List practical security basics for a Node API in production (secrets, headers, input, deps).
Why does semantic HTML matter for accessibility and SEO? Give tag examples for a blog post page.
Build (describe) an accessible signup form with labels, required fields, and useful input types.
What are 5 HTML accessibility checks you would run before shipping a marketing page?
hints: Color is not the only signal

questions.prompt: Explain the box model and how box-sizing: border-box changes layout math.
When do you choose Flexbox vs Grid? Describe a header + card gallery layout.
How would you make a page responsive using relative units and media queries without breaking desktop layout?
You are a Java engineer moving to Python. What skills transfer, what do you unlearn, and how do you stay production-safe without Java’s ceremony?
hints: Unlearn mandatory classes and getters everywhere
Mention typing + venv + tests as the safety net

questions.prompt: Map Java List and Map to Python. When do you use a comprehension, and what mutable-default pitfall must you avoid?
How do Python dataclasses and Protocol compare to Java records/Lombok and interfaces? When do you still write a full class?
Describe the Python toolchain you would require on a team coming from Maven/JUnit: environments, types, tests, and CI checks.
Compare Java ExecutorService / CompletableFuture to Python asyncio. When is asyncio the wrong tool?
hints: do not block the event loop

questions.prompt: Explain Spring Boot REST + Bean Validation as FastAPI + Pydantic. Where does business logic live, and what do you keep identical to Java service design?
